title: datamatch: Fetch Ocean Data from Several Sources and Match It in Space and Time
description:
Downloads ocean and atmosphere data and joins it to point data in space and time, at the downloaded data's own resolution. The join is a general spatiotemporal nearest-feature match, so either side may be species observations, survey stations, tag positions, or another gridded product.

Five sources are covered behind one interface and one set of variable names, so a covariate arrives in a column of the same name whichever supplied it: the Copernicus Marine Service for global reanalysis, analysis-and-forecast, satellite ocean colour and surface wind; HYCOM for an independent global model publishing sea-floor fields; FVCOM for unstructured-mesh coastal models such as NECOFS; CCMP for a long six-hourly surface wind record; and NOAA ERDDAP for high-resolution satellite sea surface temperature and chlorophyll. Which source produced each value is recorded on the result, because values sharing a column name across sources are not interchangeable.

Also provides spatial and temporal resampling for combining products of different resolution, gap filling for satellite ocean colour, seafloor terrain from NOAA ETOPO, basin-scale climate indices, plots for inspecting what was downloaded, and Ecological Metadata Language for a matched table.

The data products a given run fetches carry their own citations, which are separate from this one and also required.
